paragraphs: that one did 558 while the last two weeks did 62, 181, 373 and 107. same trader, same model, same camera.
the difference is the title. an exact number, the method named, and a bracket that promises the how. then you stopped writing them like that.
lowercase, always. the second a title goes into title case it starts sounding like a brand instead of a person, and that is the whole guru tell.

content.title: how content really works
paragraphs: content is the thing that primes everything else. packaging decides whether any of it gets seen. everything else on this page is small next to that.

the youtube link in the bio matters because a new pair of eyes gets nurtured by long form in a way a grid never does. that's the 7-11-4 rule, and youtube stacks those hours far faster than instagram ever will.

vsl.title: your vsl, rewritten
vsl.intro: you have tested a lot of these. we built you one off the limited view we have from the outside, on the framework we use for this, which has done over $10m in info product and mentorship sales. tap a step to open it.

steps.title: the hook
steps.sub: say what you'll do for them, in one line
steps.quote: I'm Berg. I'm going to teach you a mechanical day trading model you can run in about 45 minutes a day, and you'll be able to check my own results against yours the entire time.
body: no build up, no backdrop, no welcome-guys. if people drop in the first fifteen seconds, this line is the reason.

steps.title: why you
steps.sub: your story, once they know why to listen
body: where you were: 10 pip stops and 30 pip targets, no idea whether the day would be a swing or a wick.
what changed: basing entry, stop and target on the range, measured with the fib tool.
what it bought: three years profitable, 40 years of backtested data, about 45 minutes a day on the charts, nine winning months a year and three losing ones, said out loud.
the life: left open on purpose. that beat has to be yours.

steps.title: buying motives
steps.sub: why people actually come to you, most common first
body: a year or two in and still not profitable. stuck on the prop firm treadmill. can't hold a system for more than a fortnight. doing it alone. each one gets a line of its own, in the order they show up on your calls.

steps.title: the offer
steps.sub: what it is, how long, what they get, what it costs
body: the price gets said out loud. we left the number for you, it's yours to state.

steps.title: objections
steps.sub: the real ones, from your own videos
body: "i'd have to be at a laptop all day" is forty-five minutes, limit orders and phone alerts. "how long before i'm profitable" is under four weeks to teach the model and one to two years for the skill, and you say both. the rest comes from your sales calls.

steps.title: qualification and the ask
steps.sub: your own line, word for word, then one action
body: you already tell people not to apply if they won't put the hours in. that stays exactly as you said it. then one action: the application, then the call.
